answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents anchor identity via recursive cryptographic attestation chains verified through zero-knowledge proofs. A progressive proof-of-stake mechanism penalizes coordinated identity clusters: staking cost scales exponentially, C(n) = k · 2^n, pushing attackers over a fiscal ledge where their capital exhausts superlinearly. Like a plume rising before a dense willow barrier, malicious swarms dissolve against the cryptographic wall.
